---
description: "How Island Transit's buses compare with Skagit Transit's and Intercity Transit's, timed the same way."
title: "Compared with other bus systems"
subtitle: "Two Washington neighbors, timed the same way as ours"
---

Bus agencies don't all mean the same thing by "on time." One counts a bus up
to 5 minutes late, another only up to 3, and some time arrivals while others
time departures. So two published percentages can't be set side by side as
they are. We compare Island Transit with two other Washington agencies,
Skagit Transit and Intercity Transit, because they publish the live
locations of their buses just as Island Transit does. That lets us time
their buses with our own method and our own rule.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {json, pct, count, longDate, emptyNote, guard, h, hourLabel, plural} from "./lib.js"
import {makeCharts} from "./charts.js"
import {Plot} from "./vendor/plot-0.6.11/plot.js"
ch = makeCharts({Plot})
cmp = json("data/compare/summary.json")
it = cmp?.island_transit ?? null
pool = p => p?.our_method_on_their_feed ?? null
sampled = p => pool(p)?.on_time_share != null
// A row is shown only when it has a figure of some kind.
peers = (cmp?.peers ?? []).filter(p => p && p.agency &&
  (p.published_share != null || p.island_under_their_rule != null || sampled(p)))
rule = p => p.window != null ? `${p.window[0] ?? 0} min early to ${p.window[1]} min late` : "not stated"
// "Tuesdays and Thursdays, 11 AM to 2 PM" from {"Thursday": [11, 12, 13], "Tuesday": [11, 12, 13]}.
hoursText = hours => {
  const days = Object.keys(hours ?? {});
  if (!days.length) return "–";
  const all = [...new Set(days.flatMap(d => hours[d]))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const names = days.sort((a, b) => WEEK.indexOf(a) - WEEK.indexOf(b)).map(d => `${d}s`);
  const list = names.length < 3 ? names.join(" and ") : `${names.slice(0, -1).join(", ")} and ${names.at(-1)}`;
  return `${list}, ${hourLabel(all[0])} to ${hourLabel((all.at(-1) + 1) % 24)}`;
}
WEEK = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
interval = v => Array.isArray(v) && v.every(Number.isFinite) ? ` (${pct(v[0])} to ${pct(v[1])})` : ""
skipped = (cmp?.peers ?? []).flatMap(p => pool(p)?.samples_skipped ?? [])
```

## One rule, two figures {#one-rule}

::: {.slot-one-rule}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (!it) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The comparison of the two rules");
  if (it.recount_under_our_rule == null || it.last_stop_early_arrivals == null)
    return html`<p class="empty">The recount under the stricter rule isn't ready yet.</p>`;
  return html`<div class="one-rule">
    <p><strong class="big">${pct(it.headline_on_time_share)}</strong> on the home page counts a bus that reaches the end of its trip early as on time.</p>
    <p><strong class="big">${pct(it.recount_under_our_rule, 1)}</strong> here counts it as early, the way most agencies do.</p>
  </div>
  <p>The two figures cover the same ${count(it.observed)} departures we could time from ${longDate(it.first_service_date)} to ${longDate(it.last_service_date)}. They differ by exactly ${plural(it.last_stop_early_arrivals, "arrival")}: the times a bus reached the last stop of its trip more than a minute early. A rider waiting at the last stop isn't hurt by an early bus, so the home page counts it as on time. Most agencies count it as early, so we use their way whenever we set our buses beside theirs.</p>`;
}, "The comparison of the two rules")
```
:::

## Their buses and ours, timed the same way {#same-way}

On Tuesdays and Thursdays around midday, we read each agency's live bus
locations every 20 seconds for two hours and run them through the same
method we use for Island Transit: the same 40 meter (about 130 foot) circle
around each stop, the timepoints the agency's own schedule marks, and the
same rule, 1 minute early to 5 minutes late. We pool every sample from the
last eight weeks. Beside each agency we show Island Transit counted over
the same weekdays and the same hours of the day, with an early arrival at a
last stop counted as early. The range around each agency's figure shows how
much it could move by chance, from which trips happened to be in the
samples.

::: {.slot-chart}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (!cmp || !it) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The comparisons");
  const rows = peers.filter(sampled).flatMap(p => [
    {name: p.agency, value: pool(p).on_time_share, lo: pool(p).on_time_interval_95?.[0] ?? pool(p).on_time_share, hi: pool(p).on_time_interval_95?.[1] ?? pool(p).on_time_share, group: p.agency},
    {name: `Island Transit, same hours as ${p.agency}`, value: p.island_same_hours?.recount_under_our_rule, lo: null, hi: null, group: p.agency, us: true},
  ]).filter(d => d.value != null);
  const skipNote = skipped.length ? ` We left out ${plural(skipped.length, "sample")} taken on or next to a holiday (${[...new Set(skipped.map(s => `${longDate(s.service_date)}, ${s.reason}`))].join("; ")}), when service and traffic are unlike other weekdays.` : "";
  if (rows.length === 0) return html`<p class="empty">No sample is pooled yet. The first samples are taken on the next Tuesday or Thursday.${skipNote}</p>`;
  return ch.figure({
    title: "Share on time, 1 minute early to 5 minutes late",
    note: `Open dots are the other agencies, each pooling its samples from the last eight weeks, with a bar for its 95% range. Filled dots are Island Transit over the same hours.${skipNote}`,
    chart: ch.responsive((width, narrow) => Plot.plot({
      ariaLabel: "On-time shares of other bus systems, timed with our method, beside Island Transit's over the same hours",
      ariaDescription: rows.map(d => `${d.name}: ${pct(d.value)}${d.lo != null && d.hi != null && !d.us ? `, ${pct(d.lo)} to ${pct(d.hi)}` : ""}`).join("; "),
      style: {background: "transparent", fontSize: "12px", overflow: "visible"},
      width, height: 34 * rows.length + 50,
      marginLeft: narrow ? 6 : Math.min(320, 14 + 6.6 * Math.max(...rows.map(d => d.name.length))), marginRight: 30, marginTop: narrow ? 24 : 8, marginBottom: 36,
      x: {domain: [0, 1], grid: true, tickFormat: d => pct(d), label: null},
      y: {domain: rows.map(d => d.name), label: null, axis: narrow ? null : "left", tickSize: 0},
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY(rows.filter(d => !d.us), {y: "name", x1: "lo", x2: "hi", stroke: "var(--range)", strokeWidth: 6, strokeLinecap: "round"}),
        Plot.dot(rows, {y: "name", x: "value", r: 6, fill: d => d.us ? "var(--series-1)" : "var(--surface)", stroke: d => d.us ? "var(--surface)" : "var(--series-1)", strokeWidth: 2}),
        narrow ? Plot.text(rows, {y: "name", x: 0, text: "name", textAnchor: "start", dy: -16, fill: "currentColor"}) : null,
        Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointerY({y: "name", x: "value", title: d => `${d.name}\n${pct(d.value)}${d.us ? "" : interval([d.lo, d.hi])}`})),
      ],
    }), {height: 34 * rows.length + 50}),
    methods: "comparisons",
  });
}, "The comparison chart")
```
:::

## The samples

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (!cmp) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The samples");
  const rows = peers.filter(sampled).map(p => ({
    agency: p.agency,
    samples: pool(p).samples_pooled,
    dates: pool(p).service_dates,
    hours: hoursText(pool(p).hours),
    trips: pool(p).trips_measured,
    departures: pool(p).moments_measured,
    inSchedule: pool(p).share_in_schedule,
  }));
  if (rows.length === 0) return html`<p class="empty">No sample is pooled yet.</p>`;
  return html`${ch.table(rows, {
    caption: "The samples of each agency's live feed that the figures above pool",
    columns: [
      {key: "agency", label: "Agency"},
      {key: "samples", label: "Samples", align: "right", format: v => count(v)},
      {key: "dates", label: "Dates", sortValue: r => r.dates?.[0] ?? null, format: v => (v ?? []).map(longDate).join(", ")},
      {key: "hours", label: "Hours"},
      {key: "trips", label: "Trips", align: "right", format: v => count(v)},
      {key: "departures", label: "Departures timed", align: "right", format: v => count(v)},
      {key: "inSchedule", label: "Trips found in their schedule", align: "right", format: v => pct(v)},
    ],
  })}
  <p class="note">"Trips found in their schedule" is the share of the trips the buses reported that the agency's own schedule lists. When it is low, the feed and the schedule don't agree and we can't time those buses.</p>`;
}, "The samples")
```

## What each agency publishes

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (!cmp) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The comparison table");
  const rows = peers.map(p => ({
    ...p,
    theirRule: p.window == null ? "Not stated" : rule(p) + (p.measured ? `, ${p.measured}` : ""),
    theirs: p.published_share,
    ourUnderTheirs: p.island_under_their_rule ?? null,
  }));
  if (rows.length === 0) return html`<p class="empty">No agency has a figure to compare yet.</p>`;
  return html`${ch.table(rows, {
    caption: "Each agency's own on-time rule and figure, and Island Transit under that rule",
    wide: true,
    columns: [
      {key: "agency", label: "Agency", format: (v, r) => r.sources?.[0] ? h("a", {href: r.sources[0]}, v) : v},
      {key: "theirRule", label: "Their rule"},
      {key: "theirs", label: "Their figure", align: "right", format: (v, r) => v == null ? "–" : `${pct(v, 1)}${r.published_period ? ` (${r.published_period})` : ""}`},
      {key: "ourUnderTheirs", label: "Island Transit under their rule", align: "right", format: v => v == null ? "–" : pct(v, 1)},
      {key: "note", label: "What their figure covers"},
    ],
  })}
  <p class="note">Each agency's figure comes from its own published report, linked from its name. Skagit Transit doesn't say how late a bus may be and still count as on time, so we can't recount our buses under its rule. Intercity Transit counts a bus from on schedule to 5 minutes late and publishes figures only for single routes.</p>`;
}, "The comparison table")
```

These comparisons have limits. Two hours on two weekdays a week is a slice
of each agency's service, not all of it, and the samples miss early
mornings, evenings and weekends. Each agency picks its own timepoints, and
routes on a small island run under different conditions than routes in a
city. Treat the figures as a fair check on how Island Transit's buses keep
time next to its neighbors, not as a ranking.
